conviction_note: FY26 is fully pre-released ('on track ... on all metrics', 8 Oct), so the move sits in the first FY27 guide. Three sourced, public pressures land on that guide: Germany's staged excise rises for 2027-30, passed 16 Oct (Jefferies has FY27 op profit at +1.4% against +3.5% consensus and flags a guide below the street); the CEO's own warning that a lasting Middle East conflict would hit FY27 input costs and duty free; and a weaker euro. On their own they sum to -1.7. The scaled number is only -0.52 (p_up 44 x abs 4.3) for three reasons: the stock has risen about 6% through the Jefferies warning; a £1.5bn buyback and Capital Group's buying support the tape; and both prior full-year results days rose (+3.1% in 2024, +2.4% in 2025). So the lean is weak and the size is set by the scheduled guide.

FY27 £1.5bn share buyback announced, to complete by 29 Oct 2027

Medium-term (2030 Strategy, CMD March 2025) guidance reaffirmed at H1; H1 adj op profit +0.6%, adj EPS +5.3%, an H2 step-up guided; warning that a lasting Middle East conflict could weigh on input costs and on consumer demand, duty free included
Results date: 'Our Annual Results for the year ended 30 September 2026 will be announced on 17 November 2026'

new_in_release.expect: First FY27 guide (op profit, EPS, tobacco and NGP revenue, FX). The base case reiterates 'consistent with medium-term guidance' (3-5% adj op profit at constant currency). The risk is a guide toward or below the low end, on the German excise steps from 2027, Middle East input costs and US discount competition. The sign leans down, but a plain reiteration would read as relief against the Jefferies warning.
FY27 FX translation guidance: likely a headwind, since EURGBP is about 0.834 now against roughly 0.85-0.87 through most of FY26; small negative
Progressive dividend, final instalment; expected to grow in line with policy; unlikely to surprise
FY26 FCF already signalled at >£2.2bn; FY27 cash and leverage commentary unknown
FY26 lines pre-released; expected in line; worth roughly 0

positioning_check: FCA aggregated register: 1.75% disclosed net short as of 2026-11-11, unchanged from the previous read (change 0.00 pts), so shorts are neither building nor covering (https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv). Not crowded. On the long side, Capital Group lifted its stake from 11.97% to 14.07% between 14 Oct and 4 Nov (three TR-1s), alongside the company's daily buyback.

findings.finding: Germany's parliament passed staged annual tobacco excise increases for 2027-2030 on 16 Oct 2026 (pack about €8 in 2026 to €12 or more by 2030). Germany is about 15% of Imperial's group operating profit; Jefferies cut its FY27 op profit growth estimate to 1.4% against 3.5% consensus and wrote that it detects 'a risk that F27 guidance could come below street estimates'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance and outlook lines have moved this name most: the 14 Apr 2026 trading update (share losses, FX swing, guide held) closed -4.83%; the 8 Oct 2026 reaffirmation plus buyback closed +5.06%; first-guide days at FY results were +3.08% (19 Nov 2024) and +2.41% (18 Nov 2025). Yahoo daily closes: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/IMB.L?range=2y&interval=1d
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell 1.8% on the downgrade (2826p on 19 Oct), but it has since risen to about 2992p, above the pre-downgrade 2879p. That price would be falling into the print, not rising 6%, if the market expected a guide below the 3-5% framework. The short register is flat at 1.75%, so nobody has positioned for a cut. A single broker estimate is not the consensus, and the FY27 guide has not been issued.
findings.independence: The tax law itself is confirmed by German press and the Bundesrat outcome (https://steuerzahler.de/aktuelles/detail/bundesrat-billigt-hoehere-tabaksteuer-stufenweise-anhebung-bis-2030/ ; https://de.euronews.com/2026/10/16/erhohung-der-tabaksteuer-12-euro-und-mehr-fur-eine-schachtel-zigaretten). The FY27 guidance risk rests on Jefferies alone.

findings.finding: Imperial's own H1 outlook warned that the longer the Middle East conflict persists 'the more likely there could be a more meaningful impact on input costs and consumer demand, including duty free'. The CEO placed that impact in FY27 (filters, plastics, logistics). The conflict has not ended: Brent was about $108 on 2 Nov 2026, and the 8 Oct pre-close update said nothing about FY27 profit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 14 Apr 2026 update, which first raised Middle East uncertainty alongside share losses and FX, closed -4.83%. The 12 May H1, which repeated the warning but held the guide, closed +3.81%.
findings.why_not_priced: The company flagged a contingent FY27 cost headwind six months ago and has given no FY27 number since. Oil is still above $100, so the condition it named ('the longer this persists') is being met. If the market priced a cost-driven guide cut, the stock would not sit 19.5% above its level 60 sessions ago. This is macro-to-company transmission, which the company itself has stated but not quantified, so the finding is small.
findings.independence: CEO timing quote reported separately (https://tobaccoreporter.com/?p=168684). Oil level: https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil/news/580590. Shares the FY27 guide line with finding 1 but rests on a different fact.

findings.finding: Euro translation is a likely FY27 headwind: EURGBP is 0.834 on 16 Nov 2026, against roughly 0.856-0.875 for most of Imperial's FY26 (Oct 2025-Aug 2026), and Germany, Spain and the euro-denominated Distribution business are large profit pools. USD/GBP is roughly flat (1.32 now, against 1.32-1.37 in FY26).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX guidance swinging from a 2-2.5% tailwind to a comparable headwind was cited as one driver of the -4.83% on 14 Apr 2026 (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/imperial-brands-shares-fall-after-cigarette-maker-warns-of-market-share-loss-ce7e50dfd981fe27).
findings.why_not_priced: Any analyst can compute this, and the guide is at constant currency, so it is mostly priced. It is filed small because Imperial's FX guidance line has itself moved the stock before.

findings.finding: Altria's Q3 2026 (30 Oct) showed the US discount tier at 34.1% (+2.0pts year on year) and Altria's own discount shipments up 40.5% (Basic gaining discount share). That is direct price competition in the US value segment where Imperial's brands sit, although Altria also reported the industry volume decline easing to about 5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: US and German share losses drove the -4.83% on 14 Apr 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Altria rose about 6.8% on the print and the sector rallied with it. The finding is a counterparty proxy, and Imperial's own 8 Oct update claims US share gains 'in our target segments' for the same period, so the company document outweighs the proxy for FY26. It is kept small, as a pressure on the FY27 guide only.

findings.finding: Logista, consolidated as Imperial's Distribution segment, reported FY26 adj EBIT of €391m (+3.3%) on 6 Nov and guided FY27 to mid-single-digit adj EBIT growth. That is a small, already-public support for the group FY27 guide, against Distribution adj op profit falling 3.0% in Imperial's H1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to the Distribution line on its own; it is a minority of group profit (about 8%).
findings.original_quote: De cara al ejercicio 2027, el operador logístico prevé registrar un crecimiento de dígito sencillo medio en el beneficio de explotación ajustado respecto a 2026, excluyendo la variación del valor de inventarios y posibles adquisiciones.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since 6 Nov in Spanish wire copy, and Distribution is a small slice of the group, so the finding is small. Net of the rest of the company, it adds roughly 0.3-0.4pts to group op profit growth if analysts had Distribution flat.

findings.finding: Capital Group raised its Imperial stake from 11.97% to 12.03% (14 Oct), 13.09% (22 Oct) and 14.07% (4 Nov): roughly 15m shares, or about £0.45bn, bought in three weeks into the print, alongside the company's own £1.5bn buyback.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the buying is in the tape (+14.6% since 8 Oct) and agrees with the run-up. It is filed only as evidence that a large informed long holder did not read the German tax as a reason to sell.

outside_window.finding: The German excise steps take effect from 2027 (cigars, cigarillos and pipe tobacco from 1 Mar 2027); the volume effect lands in FY27 trading, not on results day
